metaDescription: Lawn mowers for hills compared on drive type, traction, weight and slope rating, from self-propelled walk-behinds to AWD robots and remote crawlers.
expertTake: The PowerSmart EasyDrive Pro 22-inch with rear-wheel drive is the best walk-behind for hills for most homeowners, the EGO LM2135SP is the cordless pick for moderate grades, and the DREAME A3 AWD is the machine to buy if you never want to walk a slope again. Skip riding and zero-turn mowers on steep ground: stability and braking become the limit.
introParagraphs: Mowing a hill is a traction and stability problem, not a power problem. Wheels have to grip wet or dry turf, the weight has to stay low and over the driven axle and the operator has to stay upright. A mower that is perfectly fine on flat ground can spin its wheels, slide sideways or tip when the grade increases.

That is why drive layout matters more than horsepower here. Rear-wheel drive, large tread, all-wheel drive on robots and tracks on remote crawlers each solve the problem differently, with their own limits. This guide compares these approaches so you can match a machine to the steepest grade on your property.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyDrive Pro 22-Inch 170cc Rear-Wheel Drive
products.description:
Rear-wheel drive is the correct answer for most walk-behind mowers on hills, and the EasyDrive Pro uses it with a 170cc overhead-valve engine. When you mow uphill, weight shifts to the rear, which loads the driven wheels and increases grip. A front-drive mower unloads its drive wheels exactly when it needs traction.

The 22-inch steel deck covers more ground per pass and the 170cc engine has enough torque for thick grass at a grade. The maker positions it for slopes and uneven terrain.

For safety on a hill, mow across the slope with a walk-behind, not up and down, and wear boots with grip. Against the EGO battery option, it has no runtime limit, but it weighs more and needs fuel and oil care. Wear boots with deep tread and keep the discharge side facing downhill.
products.bestFor: Moderate to steep residential slopes where traction is the main need.
pros: Rear-wheel drive loads the tires uphill
170cc engine has torque for thick grass
cons: Heavy to hold on a side slope

products.name: PowerSmart 21-Inch 170cc Hills and Medium Yards
products.description:
This model combines rear-wheel drive with 10-inch large wheels. Larger wheels roll over bumps and ruts without bogging and spread contact over more tread, which matters on lumpy hillsides.

The 3-in-1 deck switches between bag, mulch and discharge without tools, so you can mulch on dry grass and bag in the shoulder season. A 170cc OHV engine starts in a pull or two according to the maker, which is welcome after a long layoff.

Compared with the 22-inch EasyDrive Pro it has a narrower deck but larger wheels. Both share the engine and drive layout, so the choice is about wheel size and deck width. Check tire pressure on both sides, since a soft tire makes a hillside mower crab sideways.
products.bestFor: Bumpy hillsides where wheel size helps traction.
pros: 170cc engine with torque for thick grass

products.name: EGO Power+ LM2135SP 21-Inch Self-Propelled
products.description:
EGO's LM2135SP claims up to 7.0 foot-pounds of cutting torque, a useful comparison to gas engines, and up to 60 minutes of runtime. Touch Drive lets the handle control speed: you move your hand and the mower follows, which is easier than adjusting a lever on a slope.

With a cordless mower, weight is lower than gas, which helps on slopes, and there is no fuel or pull cord. The limit is battery energy, since self-propel draws from the same pack and slopes demand more power.

Against the PowerSmart gas models it is lighter and quieter, but needs charging between mowing sessions on big hills. Keep a spare battery for large properties. Charge a second pack before a big hillside job so you are not stranded halfway across a bank.
products.bestFor: Moderate slopes and small to medium lawns for EGO battery owners.
pros: Touch Drive makes speed control easy

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled
products.description:
Greenworks uses an 80-volt system and a brushless motor with rear-wheel drive and variable speed. Rear drive is what you want on a hill, and a brushless motor provides more torque and efficiency than older brushed designs.

The maker claims up to half an acre per charge on light grass, which will shrink on hills. The LED headlight is useful for early or late mowing.

Compared with the EGO it uses a higher voltage platform, with similar deck width. Both rely on pack capacity to determine how much slope you can mow per charge. Expect shorter runtime than the half-acre claim whenever the mower climbs.
products.bestFor: Cordless owners with moderate slopes up to a half acre.

products.name: DREAME A3 AWD 2000 LiDAR Robot Mower
products.description:
The A3 AWD is a robot designed for hilly homeowners, with all-wheel drive rated by the maker for 38.7 degrees, about 80 percent grade. LiDAR navigation maps the lawn without a wire or satellite base station, so there is nothing to bury and no signal to lose.

A 45-minute fast charge shortens the downtime between sessions. A robot removes the physical risk of mowing a hill by hand, because you never walk the grade.

The tradeoff is price tier and wet-grass traction. Slope ratings assume dry turf, and a 38.7-degree slope is far steeper than most people should walk. Keep the sensors clean and replace blades regularly. Walk the lawn first and mark soft spots or drop-offs where it should not go.
products.bestFor: Steep lawns where nobody wants to walk the slope.

products.name: INFRONT Remote Control Tracked Mower 9 HP
products.description:
A remote-controlled crawler mower removes the operator from the slope. Rubber tracks spread weight over a long contact patch, and a zero turning radius lets it pivot on steep ground. The 9 HP, 225cc gas engine has electric start.

The maker claims 45-degree climbing, a very steep angle that you should treat as a ceiling, not a working limit. Wet turf, loose soil and obstacles reduce it sharply.

It costs far more than a walk-behind and needs line-of-sight control. For banks, ditches and steep rough ground that cannot be mowed safely by hand, it is the practical option. Keep it in sight at all times and stop it before the engine labors on a climb.
products.bestFor: Steep banks and rough ground where a person should not walk.
pros: Remote control keeps you off the slope

products.name: Tyzar 27HP Gas Remote Control Tracked Mower
products.description:
The Tyzar is a commercial-style crawler: a 27 HP Loncin gas engine on a 705-pound steel chassis with tracks and a 39.7-inch cutting deck. The maker claims 28,703 to 35,880 square feet per hour and a remote range of 600 meters.

The weight is both a strength and a limit. A heavy tracked machine is stable on slopes and in ditches, but it needs a trailer and hard standing to transport. The 65-degree slope claim should be read as a marketing ceiling.

It is far more machine than a homeowner needs, and it makes sense for large banks, bushland and roadside work. Expect engine, track and cutting-head maintenance. Inspect tracks and rollers for stones before each session, since a thrown track on a slope is dangerous.
products.bestFor: Large steep banks, ditches and rough bushland.
pros: 27 HP engine with high output claim
cons: More machine than most lawns need

buyingCriteria.explanation: Going uphill, weight shifts rearward, so rear-wheel drive like the PowerSmart EasyDrive Pro and Greenworks 80V gains traction while front drive loses it. All-wheel drive on the DREAME A3 AWD and tracks on the crawlers solve the problem differently. Choose by steepest grade. A simple check is to push the mower uphill by hand with the drive off: a rear-heavy machine feels steadier.

Slope ratings are in degrees or percent: 45 degrees is a 100 percent grade, and 38.7 degrees is about 80 percent. Most walk-behind mowers are safe on modest slopes only, and manufacturers set limits near 15 degrees. Treat ratings as ceilings and leave wet-grass margin.

Large wheels, like the 10-inch ones on the PowerSmart hills model, roll over ruts and spread contact. Aggressive tread bites wet turf. Small plastic wheels spin and bounce on a hillside. Pressing a thumb into the tread shows whether it is deep enough to clear mud.
With a walk-behind, mow across a slope so a slip pulls the machine away from your feet. With a riding mower, mow up and down only where the manual allows. Robots and crawlers follow their own paths.

Hills draw more energy. A cordless mower like the EGO LM2135SP can lose a large share of its runtime on a steep lawn, so size the battery generously. Gas has no such limit. Add a spare battery to your budget before you commit to a cordless hill mower.

Keeping a person off a steep slope is a real benefit of robots like the DREAME and crawlers like the INFRONT and Tyzar. If a slope scares you, buy a machine that does not need you on it. Think about who mows when you are away: a slope you cannot walk is a slope you should automate.

specDecoder.meaning: Slope can be given as an angle or as rise over run. 45 degrees equals 100 percent. Always convert before comparing two machines.
Drive wheels at the rear gain grip when weight shifts back on an uphill climb.
A handle control that sets speed from hand position. It keeps both hands on the bar.
A laser scanner that maps the lawn with no wire or satellite base. It works in shade. It also avoids the satellite lock problems of RTK in valleys.
Continuous rubber belts that spread weight and grip. They are stable but heavy.
specDecoder.watchFor: INFRONT and Tyzar crawlers use them.

howWeEvaluated.title: Traction layout
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rear-wheel, all-wheel and track drives, giving the most credit to layouts that load the driven wheels uphill.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wheel and tread design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at wheel size and tread, noting the 10-inch wheels on the PowerSmart hills model. Large wheels and low tire pressure were treated as tradeoffs, not absolute advantages.

howWeEvaluated.title: Slope ratings
howWeEvaluated.description: We read maker ratings as ceilings. DREAME and Tyzar quote steep claims that deserve caution.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power source under load
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how hills affect battery runtime on the EGO and Greenworks, versus unlimited gas runtime. We assumed that hills use more energy than flat lawns by a meaningful margin.

howWeEvaluated.title: Operator safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored robots and crawlers higher for removing the operator from steep ground, while noting their price and complexity.

rows: AWD and no operator on the grade

cards.label: Walk-behind
cards.text: The PowerSmart, EGO and Greenworks models are affordable and you control them, but you walk the slope.

cards.label: Robot or crawler
cards.text: The DREAME A3 AWD, INFRONT and Tyzar keep you off the grade, but cost far more and need setup or line of sight.

howToChoose.note: Pick a walk-behind for moderate slopes, a robot or crawler for steep or hazardous ground.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for aggressive tread, large wheels and low weight over the driven axle. Avoid mowing wet slopes by hand where possible.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The PowerSmart hills model's 10-inch wheels and rear drive help, and tracked crawlers hold best on slick turf.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if the slope is steep or dangerous, which points to the DREAME A3 AWD or a tracked crawler.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if the slope is gentle. The PowerSmart EasyDrive Pro handles it at a lower price.

maintenance.task: Check wheel tread and tire pressure
maintenance.why: Worn tread loses grip on hills. Keep pressure even for a straight track.
A dull blade strains the engine or battery, which matters on slopes.
Gas engines run hotter on grades. Fresh oil protects bearings.
Dirt blinds robot sensors and clogs track rollers.
Keep lithium packs at partial charge.

faq.q: How steep is too steep for a walk-behind?
faq.a: Manufacturers usually set limits near 15 degrees. If you cannot keep your footing, the slope is too steep and a robot or crawler is safer.

faq.q: Should I mow up and down or across?
faq.a: With a walk-behind, mow across so a slip moves the mower away from your feet. With a riding mower, follow the manual.

faq.q: Are electric mowers good on hills?
faq.a: Yes, they are light and quiet, but hills drain batteries faster. Keep a spare.

faq.q: Do robot mowers handle steep lawns?
faq.a: Models with all-wheel drive, like the DREAME A3 AWD, are rated for steep grades, but wet grass reduces traction.

faq.q: Is a remote-control crawler worth it?
faq.a: For steep banks or ditches that cannot be mowed safely by hand, yes. For ordinary lawns it is overkill.

faq.q: Can I use a zero-turn on a hill?
faq.a: Only on gentle slopes. Braking and traction are limited, so follow the maker's slope limit.
